gbm_population_evidence.quote: Participants must have histologically World Health Organization Grade IV IDH wildtype glioblastoma by IDHR132H immunohistochemistry or variants including gliosarcoma or IDH wildtype diffuse glioma with molecularly features of glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: Merck Sharp \& Dohme Corp., a subsidiary of Merck \& Co., Inc., is supporting this research study by providing funding for the research study and both investigational study drugs, pembrolizumab and olaparib.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Participants must be at first or second relapse of GBM.

tumour_pk_planned_evidence.quote: For the first 10 patients in Arm A who will have tumor resected for analysis of olaparib levels, both enhancing and non-enhancing tumor should be available for resection.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: TIL density quantifies anti-tumor immune response. It is measured in tumor tissue from protocol surgery, analyzed by immunohistochemistry and by next generation sequencing.

role_evidence.quote: This is an open label, multi-center, phase II trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of olaparib, temozolomide and pembrolizumab in participants with recurrent glioblastoma at their first or second relapse.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not approved pembrolizumab or olaparib for recurrent glioblastoma, but both have been approved for other uses.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Pembrolizumab is an antibody designed to block the action of the receptor, PD-1.
arms: Cohort 1 (Safety Lead In): pembrolizumab plus olaparib and temozolomide
Cohort 2 (Surgical Cohort): Arm A - Pembrolizumab plus olaparib and temozolomide
Cohort 2 (Surgical Cohort): Arm B - Pembrolizumab monotherapy

role_evidence.quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not approved pembrolizumab or olaparib for recurrent glioblastoma, but both have been approved for other uses.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Olaparib helps kill cancer cells by preventing PARP from repairing their DNA.
arms: Cohort 1 (Safety Lead In): pembrolizumab plus olaparib and temozolomide
Cohort 2 (Surgical Cohort): Arm A - Pembrolizumab plus olaparib and temozolomide

role_evidence.quote: The U.S. FDA has approved temozolomide as a treatment option for glioblastoma.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Temozolomide is a chemotherapy drug that can enter the brain and prevent tumor cells from growing by causing DNA damage.
arms: Cohort 1 (Safety Lead In): pembrolizumab plus olaparib and temozolomide
Cohort 2 (Surgical Cohort): Arm A - Pembrolizumab plus olaparib and temozolomide

coder_notes: Pembrolizumab and olaparib are both called investigational study drugs; coded experimental_combination. In Cohort 2 Arm B pembrolizumab is given alone (role there would be experimental_monotherapy). Temozolomide (established GBM therapy) is a partner in Cohort 1 and Arm A only, at a 7-day/21-day schedule with olaparib; coded soc_backbone as background chemotherapy, though it is not in all arms (alternative: established_therapy_experiment); not a candidate either way. Arm B (pembrolizumab alone, labelled experimental) is the randomised reference for Arm A but is not standard of care, so control_arm_from_other_arms coded no. Tumour olaparib levels planned in resected tissue (tumour PK yes); window-of-opportunity surgery with TIL density and GEP in tumour tissue (target engagement yes for pembrolizumab). IDH-wildtype and 1p/19q/molecular GBM features are diagnostic definitions, not candidate-matched.
